Pros:
Cisco is still a good company, good starting salary and weekend shift loading, it gave equal opportunity for engineer to make the same amount regardless their grade.

the bonus is ok, better than those promisesbutneversee company.

Training and material is great, you will find lots of stuff to learn and grow you technical skills.
Cons:
the rewarding scheme is poor, engineers are working long hours and extra miles to reach the MBO, but not getting rewarded.

the pay raise is nonexistent.

very hard to get promotion.

Pros: Really interesting work. Good work life balance, depending on your current project and how much you worry about securing a system in the time you're given. Surprised at the group we've been able to hire and mostly keep. Smart, hard working coworkers you will always be learning from.
Cons:
Cisco doesn't give our group enough budget for promotions or raises to retain people. Talks a lot about how awesome we are, how appreciated our work is, fails to prove that.

Trusted to take on more and more responsibility but not good enough for promotion. Less and less time to look at more and more complex projects, while being expected to offer more help to the groups we work with and do more secondary tasks.

Pros:
Company overall does amazing things for communities around them, the environment and social justice. Also provide employees the ability to engage and contribute here.
Good opportunity for internal movement, advancement not as much.
There are A LOT of great people here, and learning new things on a daily basis is constant and rewarding.
Cons: Recent leadership changes have affected culture. There are many areas of the business where driving outcomes is done at expense of the people/team members. Decision making is becoming much less transparent. Favorites are protected and enabled.

Pros:
Great People to work with who are very knowledgable about technology, business processes and back office systems.

Cisco is supportive of it's employees learning new things, and in some instances will even pay a portion of the fees associated in obtaining an advanced degree.

Cisco provides more flexibility in working from home or in the office than any other company I know of.
Cons:
Promotions are few and opportunities for advancement are limited.  

Compensation doesn't keep pace with promotions, I know of people promoted to director who received fairly limited pay increases.

Additionally I recently hired someone and was apalled by the level of compensation they receive compared to peers.

Pros: One of the best ''schools'' in the world for new technologies. It was like a river of knowledge that just kept on flowing and flowing, and would never run dry.
Cons: Some people feel frustrated when they see you succeed and get better results than them. So they will do all they can do make your life miserable, including bullying you and say all sorts of lies to get others to dislike you as well. It takes a lot of strength of character to handle that and come away with your Dignity intact, but it's possible, because I did it.

Pros:
I started at Cisco through the awardwinning Cisco Sales Associates Program CSAP and the amount of investment that Cisco put in to transform us into Ciscograde engineers was unbelievable. There is always help around the corner only if you remember to ask!

As an Associate Systems Engineer, I was trained on Cisco's vast portfolio including Enterprise, Security, Data Center and Collaboration tools. We were encouraged to complete CCNA and CCNP certifications.

The worklife balance is probably the best thing about Cisco, next only to it's multicultural workforce. 

Shoutout again to CSAP that makes Cisco one of the best places to start your career at.
Cons: Leadership changes mean changes in the goals we're trying to achieve but in a dynamic industry like ours, I believe that's a necessity.

Pros: Cisco has not given up yet. There are enough experienced people to know how to get through tough times. Cisco has a solid run rate that could last them 20 years, key will be to keep the long view, like they had in the 90s
Cons: There is no top down leadership any longer. There has been a culture of consensus that anyone can say no but no one is able to make a decision. There is little to no upward mobility due to the hangeroners that believe that selling boxes is the only way. The engineering is right Cisco foundation has been lost.

Pros:
Flexible working hours with great worklife balance
Work from home option is one of the biggest facility this company provides and there is hardly any micro management
Cons:
Hard to manage work life balance
Very big company with constant changes

Pros: Good Salary, great bonus if you are Tech Lead or higher, benefits are okay.
Cons: Employees and management are very risk adverse and innovation is not commonplace.

Pros: Fast paced.  Challenging.  Most finance people are very intelligent, knowledgeable and highly professional.  Teams typically are very collaborative and work to help all succeed.
Cons:
You never know when Cisco will outsource your job, downsize or exit your business.  So all constantly worry when their last day will be.

Very little investment in training finance people.  Internal job rotation program is not actively managed well so movement is slow as people are afraid to change jobs for fear to lose their job.

Finance teams are a reporting function to enable management by numbers.  Finance organization needs to really and truly be value add to their business partners rather than managing their business partners like Monday morning quarterbacks.

Pros: Cisco has long been the standard for great technology companies to work for and I've loved my jobs at Cisco for quite some time. Competitive compensation, benefits, and semiannual bonus potential as well as good mobility and career path opportunities. The management and leadership culture puts priority on their people and in my experience at least, is very supportive.
Cons:
1. Not as many fun company events as there used to be, but it's all part of evolving priorities of a large company feeling the need to be socially responsible.
2. Like with any large publicly traded company, there are periodic restructurings layoffs as the whims of Wallstreet impact the business.

Pros: Knowledge sharing is key.  Everyone is open to help out.  It is great in this industry to have access to the origin of new technologies and get your hands on anything you need.
Cons: As the company grows, cisco culture is being lost.  I am happy here though, the grass isn't always greener on the other side.

Pros: If anyone wants to accelerate their career, you need not look elsewhere. CSAP is one of the most rewarding experiences I've ever had. It's tough because they expect a lot from you, but if you do your job and work hard you will be just fine. CSAP was like college all over again for me! You meet so many young professionals and hop in to those same sales/technology classes based on your track engineer or sales representative. I went through the engineer track and got put into customer role plays, shadowing opportunities with field teams, passing required exams, and half a year of classes. I've learned so much from all my mentors and peers, and these learned traits will stick with me for the rest of my life!
Cons: None! Be ready to study!

Pros: Highly dynamic, collaborative company. Depending upon which org and leadership one is under there are great opportunities to have your voice heard and help shape direction. Lots of opportunity and resources to evolve skills.
Cons: With being agile and dynamic there's often questions about direction and how to measure success. Many layers of specialists due to complexity of portfolio.

Pros: The benefits are good, the ability to work from home considering much of work is accomplished in conference calls / WebEx sessions is a nice plus, some of the newer offices are nice. Compensation is good. Work/life balance is pretty decent work from home, using devices to connect. Gym and medical center at the San Jose campus is very nice and is a great perk for local employees.
Cons: Hypercompetitive environment encourages bad business behavior and investment choices. Insular and nepotistic management at senior levels. Cultlike 'love' of the CEO. Cafes are pretty good, but prices are high. Free snacks / drinks eliminated in costcutting back in 2009 could save more cost by not rewarding the underperforming senior management :.

Pros: Great company and full of talented people.  Great compensation and benefits.  Everyone loves John Chambers and Gary Moore and SVP management is solid.  Hard working but well rewarding.
Cons: It's getting to be a large company so politics are pretty much a part of the business.  Starting to lose the difference between perception of and getting actual work done.  Repeated layoffs have demoralized the employees.  The company is going through the biggest transformation and it will be interesting to see if they succeed.

Job Title: Financial Analyst In The Lift Program
Pros: Cisco is a great company to work for. The company provides numerous opportunities to learn and grow. I have thoroughly enjoyed my time in the LiFT Leaders In Finance and Tech Program as well. This program pushes me to reach my full potential,has introduced me to a variety of people, and has provided me the opportunity to have rotations in both finance and accounting. I can't imagine working for another company other than Cisco.
Cons: Honestly, I can't think of any major cons of the company or the program. Granted, I have had to work with some difficult people in the past, but that is the case with all companies, and if anything, has taught me how to work with a variety of people.

Pros: Offered good experience in SaaS software.
Cons: Top and next level management at WebEx are clueless.  They bounce back and forth like a pingpong ball.  They are unable to develop and execute cohesive product roadmaps, yet they fool themselves into believing they can.  Employees are discouraged from bringing up "sensitive issues" to management.  Employees are encouraged to "not rock the boat."  Marketing department is unable to commit to project deadlines, yet blame this on others all the time.  Take responsibility for making things happen?  That's not a Cisco WebEx strongpoint.

Pros: Cisco was a great place to work. Too many perks to list. Leadership generally lived by the core principles of the Cisco "People Deal", an initiative to retain talent by putting the needs of employees first. One example  I was supported through a very difficult and extended personal leave. Cisco retained my job and welcomed me back once the crisis was past.
Cons: Engineeringdriven company with scattered UX practice and greatly varying levels of success. There are pockets of great design in various BUs, but unfortunately I was not in one of them. 8 bosses in 5 years, and the only excellent and fully competent one I had was fired because she rubbed some oldtimers the wrong way.

Pros: a good place to start a career, learn a lot in a short time. Company well managed with the pandemic. Mandatory working from home.
Cons:
High rotation between engineers, managers, PMs, plus layoffs every 6months then rehiring... Difficult to change internally position. Need to know with whom to be a friend in order to get a promotion. Everything depends on visibility how popular you are. Lack of transparency. Heard plenty of internal issues with managers: emotional distress, inequality. Employees afraid of talking about it loudly. Officially we were told to care of ourselves but due to the lack of a workforce, everyone is overloaded. Some managers don't allow to register overtime. So, you might land working 50h per week. 
Foreigners do not stay long, due to cultaral maching with Polish work culture.

Pros: I joined Cisco in 1995 and left in 2014.  The company I joined was not the company I left.  The culture of family existed in the 1990's and early 2000's.  The products, technologies, and people were fantastic and still are very good.
Cons: Cisco now does what large companies do, which is annual layoffs.  Sometimes these layoffs are actually ongoing just aren't reported as they are below 3% of the total employee population.  This systemic issue leads to a culture of CYA and backstabbing, especially at executive levels.

Pros:
Checking all the boxes related to social justice and D & I
Chuck is a great face for the company
Cons:
NO clear strategy that is executed with any priority/investment commitment 
Multiple layoffs due to lack of portfolio and wfp
Little career/promo opportunity if you aren't part of the 'deck' that continues to get shuffled at the top
EXTREMELY slow

Pros: The attitude of "customer success" is very prevalent within the company, so if you run up against a roadblock, using that magic phrase opens many doors.
Cons: In Customer Advocacy, there were no real opportunities for advancement unless you were willing to relocate to San Jose.  Benefit costs increased substantially every year, but there were no raises to be had.  Reorganization happened every 6 months, so I never had the same boss for one full review cycle.  Management was constantly trying to justify the existence of our group by adding supplemental job tasks to the job description, but failing to recognize and evangelize the inherent value of our core deliverables.

Pros: Great culture, great security, very smart people. It's a high integrity company with high integrity people. Very peoplefriendly place to work.
Cons: Neverending reorganizations make it extremely difficult to get anything done. Lots of decisions seem to be made based on politics and personal favors, and those decisions don't last. The result is lack of trust w/ the most executive leadership.

Pros: The best Cisco offers is flexibility in working hours.  Lots of options in when and where to work from.  Home and different locations.  Other benefits aren't the best but are acceptable.
Cons: Downside is the flexibility in working hours can sometime end up causing you to work extra long hours especially when under a time crunch.  Cisco has a fully outsourced manufacturing.  As such, many of the manufacturing operation has long since moved to lower cost regions.  This resulted in the need to work odd hours considering that time zone differences.  This can at times be a strain when new products are being launched.

Pros: An ambitious company with its heart in the right place. Capable of producing incredible technology. Pay and conditions are excellent and you get the sense that you work for a company that is not out to screw its employees. Company has a very high reputation that is, in my opinion, well deserved.
Cons: Despite working for a networking company, communication between functions can leave a lot to be desired. Company is known for being inflexible towards its customers. The overall strategy and direction can sometimes come across as being a little vague.

Pros: Challenging work which contributes to a lot of learning and growing as an employee and as a person.  Working there twenty years ago when the business was booming, was a fantastic, one time life experience.  There are a lot of smart people at Cisco, which was a great environment to work in.
Cons: They lost focus of the most important asset, people.  It is a very top and bottom organization/company.  The executive compensation gap compared to 55% of the company, is HUGE.  There should have been more key leadership changes at the very top, much much much sooner and often.

Pros:
Transparent leadership decision making
The best technology in the world
Fantastic work experience, from offices to how they equip you remotely
Focus on YOU as an employee, not what you do in a current role
High ability to move around, try new things and grow new skills
Every employee has a voice, and it is listened to
Working with the smartest, talented team in the world, around the world
Cons: some times the work from anywhere, anytime does encroach on personal life, especially if your team is global.  That said, the expectation is you are responsible for this   and take time back for yourself another occasion.

Pros:
The perks are good but thats about it. There is a the all famed claim that "Cisco is a big company" but that is all that happens.

From the day you join till end you hear the same dialogue again and again.Everything is an aquired project and no one has a clue about bringing it to ship shape quality.

The cafeteria is even outsourced so to speak and it was the worst caterers ive ever seen in my life. The people raise complains all the time but its of no use.

Occasionally theres a fire drill for which we need to run downstairs , thats one thing i learnt from there
Cons:
sick management
lack of vision
no proper management or visionary views
no guidance or mentoring in moulding new employees into anything

Pros:
Very innovative company always coming out with new products and services
 Wide community and people really willing to help out
 Compensation is amazing
 Lots of benefits, like free internet at home, free drinks at offices
 Flexibility, ability to work from home
Cons:
lack of career growth and advancement, you often get stuck with the job position and salary that you started with
 harder to transition into new and more challenging roles
 too sales focused

Pros: Fun work environment, flexible work hours and spaces, great customers to work with.  For a long time Cisco had a great strategy and moved into innovative areas, but the economy crashed and Cisco had to refocus.
Cons: We ran out of products and our BUs bacame too political and lost their mojo.  They lost all the good people and have been left with subpar PMs and others.   Cisco's had a series of layoffs and has demoralized the company.  Cisco has exited a number of businesses and is more of an R&S company as opposed to a true communications company.

Pros: It has an up and coming internship program that seems focused on attracting new hires.  If you are able to take part in the Cisco choice program you are given a decent level of flexibility in choosing which group you would like to work for.
Cons: It is a large company and it seems like it would be hard to advance positions.  I think this is a characteristic of most tech companies though.  I have been told the best way to get a raise or advance is to get a job at another company.

Pros: Amazing, talented people with a passion and mission for changing the world. Culture that supports growth, reinvention, innovative ideas. A strong vision that places listening, partnerships and advocacy for the customer at the heart of everything we do.
Cons: Yes we're big but anyone who can connect/collaborate will thrive. Yes we have too much process in places but anyone who is curious, respectfully disrupts and seeks constant improvement will be valued. Yes change is constant here but leading companies transform with a purpose. And that's how we roll.

Pros:
LIFT's rotational aspect gives you an opportunity to try 4 different roles within finance for 6 months each
 The people at Cisco are AMAZING. LIFT provides a great community of active LIFTers, LIFT alumni, and LIFT managers 
 LIFT has many great opportunities to grow your career and build your network outside of just your role, including mentor circles, networking events, additional training academies, social events, leadership series, and learning series
Cons: You are making a commitment to be held to higher standards, be engaged, and fufill various program requirements if you join this program. I don't consider that a con because that is something I wanted, but if that's not something you're willing to do, this may not be the best option for you

Pros: Flexibility, industry leader, empowering, focused on continuing education and employee resource development. You get out of the experience what you put into it from what I've seen. There is room for growth and advancement but you must work for it. Training opportunities are nearly limitless  company provided distance learning, publications, classroom based training, you name it.
Cons: Visibility, disconnection, isolation. Working with so many great people in such a disconnected environment remote/travelling/telecommuting presents challenges to gaining visibility. The distributed nature of the job lends to a feeling of disconnection to the chain of command occasionally.

Pros: Technology for routers and switches are still the best, John Chambers is a great salesman and a good leader in terms of taking care of the customers.  The growth for the early years was great.
Cons: Cisco bought quite a few consumer lines that did not really bring in considerable revenues.  There are way too many VPs,  directors, and managers in the company and their contribution should be cross examined and evaluated.

Pros: Energetic, Caring, Understanding management. One of the best places in the world to work for.  Love the environment and people. Very helpful work environment, team oriented, Vast suppositories of knowledge available for all.
Cons: kind of a weird schedule depending on which one you are assigned to at the time. No rest for the weak at heart.

Pros:
WorldClass Campus here @ Cessna Park with many lots of amenities.  
Plethora of opportunitiesIf you dont like: Development, you literally have many windows open for you. DevTest, TAC, TME, Technology Change SP>DC>Wireless etc. 
Free Internet reimbursement
Reachability to Technical Champs across the globe Fellows, DEs & PEs.
Mentoring sessions are awesome.
Flexible work hour Options, WFH
Cons:
can be better to meet Other Tech Companies:
No CAPs/hikes/Promotions from the past Year
Salary is: ~30% Less compared to SFT, Amazon.
Too Many BU Transitions

Pros: Great people to work with. Everyone is very friendly, collaborative and professional. Minimal political nonsense. Most people seem to work from home at least one day a week, so there is a good work/life balance as well. Many people who work here stay for years, and I can see why.
Cons: A lot of stakeholders involved in projects. This can delay and overcomplicate projects that could be more efficiently handled. Need fewer decision makers on some projects to eliminate unnecessary complexity. Additionally, this is the sort of company where it takes a few years at minimum to move up the ladder.

Pros: Challenging and interesting work; I have never gotten bored and the company does not suffer complacency.
Cons: Managing a work/life balance is challenging.  There is always more to do, more to learn, etc.  It is your job to manage your time and the expectations of your manager, coworkers, and customers.

Pros:
great virtual work policy....work where you please
great tools for collaborating, especially Jabber IM and WebEx
exciting to work for a major company that helps shape the tech industry
Good severance if you are let go in the layoff, ahem, limited restructuring
Cons:
Horrendously unstable
Bad communications with employees
So much lost time and effort wiped out each time layoffs; teams spend years developing great process and tools and then its all wiped out in a few weeks
Employee paranoia  when's the next cut coming

Pros: Cisco as a company provides a lot of incentives for employees  be it from the flexibility of WFH even pre COVID times to bonuses/ appraisals. Cisco management allows you to be flexible with your work  they don't encourage a strict clock in time, thereby gives you a good worklife balance.
Cons: Might not be the most exciting work for young designers and Cisco products that are developed in India are not really given enough investments or opportunities to do innovations. The designer to engineer ratio is extremely low compared to other companies. Also, the pay may not really onpar with other B2B companies and definitely lesser than what B2C companies pay.

Pros: Flexibility, great pay, innovative and good people
Cons: No annual appraisals so managers can do what they want, most upper management has no clue about the bad moral, no promotions, no stock options, no recognition

Pros: Cisco is a very diverse in technologies company and the opportunity to work across these differing technologies is amazing though results are rare. There are many very smart people, with broad backgrounds, who can offer excellent insight into many things. The overall balance of compensation/benefits/worklife are all very good.
Cons:
Cisco's primary innovation engine is acquisition, thus there are limited internal opportunities for big thinking.
Strict P&L management of business units makes it difficult for their respective GMs to invest in the future vs cost optimization.

Pros: Great employee benefits; global presence; strong ecosystem and brand name
Cons: CEO has been lost around 20062007 that caused CDO Charlie left the company; a lot of politics and fat;  doesn't have any succession plan;  can't retain talents seems CEO and board don't even care;  no innovation but still think things will turn around.  It's sad to see this will become another DEC or Sun Microsystems.

Pros: Getting to use the latest conferencing technology. Great people to work with.  Flexibility to work from home.
Cons: Don't make offers quickly enough to contractors that are exceeding expectations, recent layoffs were terrible and of great concern to people remaining.  One person doing 3 different titles, not fair for work life balance, everyone there complains they've gained weight since joining there so fitness club shouldn't be an added expense and should be a mandatory daily activity and for free.

Pros: Work from home as needed; interesting people, great pay.
Cons:
Senior Management no longer cares about its people. Every year decisions on people's lives are made and great employees are laid off without even consulting with their immediate managers. There is fear to speak up: transparency is a myth. 
There are VPs that are only in for their own selfish reasons and will lie if needed. This is no longer a company I respect.

Pros: Great place to work low key in a supportive environment. Great worklife balance. Very results oriented and collaborative – you do better work when you network pun intended with other people in the company and work strategically, rather than do headsdown grunt work. Of course this all depends on who you have as a manager, but generally the bad apples find their way out of the company in due time.
Cons: Low pay compared to similar roles in similar companies. Opportunities for increased compensation are scant, and when they do happen, its small. Career growth is at a snail's pace. This is a place to chill, not grow your career or skillset, or makes lots of money.

Pros:
Cisco creates and leverages tons of tools that make it easy to work from anywhere in the world, such as remote access devices and software, as well as revolutionary videoconferencing software TelePresence.
 Cisco employees are some of the best in the industry, and it's nice to work with smart people.
 Cisco compensates employees well, at least with salary and bonus.
Cons:
Cisco's openness to working anywhere often means you will work more hours than you otherwise would in the office.
 Retirement package is not very generous.
 Cisco did away with merit pay increases many years ago, so there's no annual compensation increases.

Pros: Good place, always on the leading edge, conducive learning environment, flexible work hours but meetings pretty much happen all the time, and if you are working with remote/offshore teams, you pretty much don't have a life as at least 3 days in a week you will have latenight calls or early morning meetings.
Cons: Working extra hours from home with remote/offshore teams is not adequately reflected in your compensation/recognition  it is almost taken for granted that you will be 24/7 on the job.

Pros: telecommuting from work, flexibility which means roundtheclock at times, friendly people all over, compensation is onpar if not better than its competitors, transparency
Cons: playing catchup while pushing its weight on to competitors, employee morale low due to 'limitedrestructuring', no one dares to challenge the status quosome did and was sidelined, general prospects are gloomy, not a great place for young people, geny, millennials

Pros: Great company, good benefits, great people, dynamic place
Cons: Don't plan on making Cisco a career employer, they target employees 5 + and the sad part is, they tell you "it wasn't performance related".   "Workforce reductions" are base on how much you make an tenure.  I've seen excellent people let go, only to bring in contractors and be rehired as a contractor.

Pros:
The people were passionate, smart, helpful and forward thinking
 Being part of a company that has such a huge impact across the globe 
 I personally loved the flexibility and working from home
 Networking....it seems like anywhere you go after Cisco there are tons of exCisco people which instantly bonds you
 Amazing benefits!
Cons:
Constant layoffs make it hard to stay aligned with your goals and even know what you job is at times. Sometimes you also wonder how they make some of their decisions on who to keep and who to let go
 Because the company is so large, it can feel like the work you do is just a drop in the bucket
 Collaborative work spaces

Pros: Good benefits and multiple business units to join. Teams focus on meeting goals. Management comes up from the ranks. You can learn as much as you can take in. Lots of business unit with different products that will keep your interest.
Cons: Depending on the teams, diversity is not always apparent. People tend to hire and work with same ethnic which doesn't promote diversity nor cohesiveness and somewhat of a prejudice environment if you are not the same ethnic.

Pros: Flexible work schedule. Decent PTO, average benefits
Cons: The Security and Government part of Cisco can't call it a division because they don't like that word is completely leaderless. Sure, they have people who fill those positions but they provide absolutely zero leadership. The senior management is aloof and does not directly communicate with or engage the workforce.

Pros:
Great team.
Top talent.
Cuttingedge, ever changing and evolving.
Pays well.
Great benefits package, including matching 401K and stock options.
Cisco Health services, with monetary reward for participating.
Able to work from home. Great for worklife balance.
Cons:
Too many cooks in the kitchen on any given product or project.
Upper management doesn't really understand what individual contributors do.
All profit driven, very little room for creativity.
Persistent reorganization and layoffs creates an environment of dogeatdog and fear.

Pros: Good benefits.  Flexible workplace is fantastic.  Depending on the team, great colleagues.
Cons: Lots of talk, little want to actually change.  Toxic managers who are managers, not leaders and don't want others to succeed, only make their team look good.  Promotion of the best looking and nonteam playing members.  Not really free to take risks, fail and learn.  Lots of bureaucracy, red tape, and processes slowing down decisions, etc. Lot more, "Tried and true, vs. innovate and new".

Pros:
Great support for new hires out of college
 Excellent leadership team that really cares about employees and their wellbeing
 Internal mobility is highlighted and personal development is supported by your team
 Great work/life balance has been especially apparent during Covid WFH

Pros: Cisco has historically been a great place to work. Management does care about the employees and their personal well being. The work is challenging and can be satisfying and rewarding. More recently with the troubles in Cisco's business the company is changing for the worse. There has been massive attrition of key engineers and engineering leaders and Cisco doesn't seem to be able to stop this trend. While the company is certainly not a disaster and the problems it faces are recoverable it needs to move quickly and decisively which is something it has not been able to do for the past 3+ years since it implemented the boards and councils management structure a mistake John Chambers is directly responsible for. Since then most of this structure has been removed and now its about getting the right leaders in place. Compensation is relatively fair especially if you have a good manager who recognizes who the contributors are. Benefits are really good to...
Cons: Attrition is a major issue right now and Cisco needs to stop the bleeding quickly and figure out not only how its going to retain the top talent but attract new talent which is especially difficult in Silicon Valley where there are many startups wooing the top talent as well as employees leaving to join the red hot social networking companies. You need talented engineers to build the best products and solutions in the market and while this won't effect the company in the next 12  18 months you will see the impact outside of that. The executive team is a group of extremely bright and talented business people but that is also the biggest problem is that there are no true Engineers at the top of the company and this is a technology company who needs great executive technology leadership!

Pros: Great people. Good community. Great use of own technology to enable collaboration and anywhere, anytime, any device connectivity. Home office setup was great!

Pros: Lots of people with families and CEO John Chambers fosters a familyatmosphere. While you can put in lots of hours, stress levels are kept pretty low. We get the job done, but we don't' run over people to do it. Great benefits including the company medical facility in San Jose and employee Gym. Very smart people here and it's bay area. Traditionally a strong rotation culture but see cons list on this one. Generous bonuses. You also get a frontrow seat on some pretty awesome technology and vision for the future.
Cons:
Cisco does a terrible job identifying talent and promoting them, as a result of this and the recent layoffs and market challenges, I think Cisco is seeing a bit of a brain drain. I know and hear of plenty of notable talent heading for the doors. one reason they're leaving is this company prefers outside talent to fill open positions which clogs the top and greatly limits upward mobility. While traditionally a rotation company, which is great, open reqs have been almost all shut down coupled with the new focus of hiring in RTP North Carolina complicates and limits available rotations in San Jose. 
There's also very limited equity adjustments and a weak mechanism for distribution. After several years I learned new hires at my same level were being offered salaries higher than my own. That tells me Cisco values my time here less than brand new people and is the completely wrong message. Another gentle push out the door.

Pros:

You will be working on pertinent projects with fulltime employees, doing the same [if not similar] things they're doing. If your team is busy, you'll be busy too.

There's an "opendoor" culture at work  if you have questions or concerns, you are free to bring it up to your manager or coworkers. Many of them are more than willing to help you learn and contribute while you're here.
Cons:
If you're not a local, relocating to San Jose can be confusing. Although Cisco offers relocation compensation, it'll be up to you to find a place to live for the next 3 to 6 months. "Corporate housing" is not offered for interns and coops. However, the Silicon Valley area has seen so many interns/temps that many neighborhoods/apartments offer shortterm or monthtomonth leases.

This might not seem like a "con" especially if you're a college student, but if your team needs you to stay until midnight to get something done, expect to do so and expect overtime pay as well.

Despite my short stay, I have definitely caught a whiff of the stagnating bureaucracy that can drive you, your project, and your coworkers nuts. But I suppose this is what happens in a "big company."

Job Title: Web Project Lead (Title Has Little To Do With My Real Job)
Pros: I just passed my 10 year anniversary and am still proud to work at Cisco. The benefits are varied and quite good, lots of vacation earned 6.16 hrs / pay period and caps at 280 hours. Lots of nonmonetary rewards like gymnasium, child care, dry cleaning, car wash, new medical facility, free soda and water although not for long, and telecommuting options although this varies greatly by group and manager, the pay for my monthly home broadband too $62/month. Lots of online education and the tuition reimbursement is great $7500/year. Fortunately I work in a fairly decent group marketing with minimal politics except for a few highly volitle people. I have an engineering background so like the mix of business and technical. If you're a technical person, it's a pretty good gig.
Cons:
I don't know where the many people who wrote reviews here work who said there is good work/life balance because I've never seen it. I have never worked less than 55 hrs/week and often 80+ hrs.  There absolutely are duds here who are great at talking nonstop and so get recognized but they don't do anything. I get frustrated working at a high tech company and constantly get asked stupid questions about how to use Excel or PowerPoint or things they can easily look up themselves. How can someone get a job here and not know computer basics is beyond me. Just because they're busy doesn't mean they're productive basic computer skills would be a great improvement.

I also don't like the performance review system which many others mentioned. It's an absolute joke and not a good one. Your score has little to do with the quality of your work, but how much your manager likes you, how much work s/he is willing to do to help you get ahead, and how lazy they are. I've had managers tell me they never give an X the highest score no matter what you do and everyone gets the same rating because it's easier for the manager. I was fortunate to finally get a promotion last year and two raises but it was a horrific, buttkissing process. I've had over 15 CAP awards over the years but none of that seems to matter. You can do the exact same work for manager A and get a E score but then move to manager B and get an X, it makes no sense and there is no oversight or standards.
